visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A middle-aged man with short gray hair and glasses is the central figure, standing against a composite background. He wears a dark button-down shirt. His facial expressions are animated, frequently using hand gestures to emphasize points while holding a small black remote or pointer. Behind him, to the right, is a large, high-resolution image of a tabby cat yawning widely with its mouth open, showcasing its teeth and tongue. The background also includes a blurred image of a living room setting with a couch. The lighting is bright and studio-like, focusing on the man. (2) The scene shifts to a technical diagram on a white background. The diagram labeled (a) shows initial state preparation, various labeled blocks like U, Perturb, and BLEW-12, and a butterfly icon. Below it, section (b) displays a sequence of molecular structures consisting of benzene rings with attached atoms numbered 1 to 4. The man's hands occasionally appear in the lower frame, pointing towards the diagram with a pen. The background is clean and clinical. (3) The man returns to the foreground, continuing his expressive delivery. He gestures with his hands, holding the remote and a pen. The background still features the yawning cat image on the right and the blurred indoor scene on the left. His facial expressions shift between serious explanation and slight smiles. (4) The man is centered, wearing the same dark shirt and glasses. He is very active with his hands, pointing and moving them to match his speech. The yawning cat remains a prominent visual element in the background. The lighting remains consistent and clear on the subject. (5) A new technical diagram appears. Labelled (c), it shows a flow chart comparing NMR experiment data with Quantum computer simulation data, leading to Feedback and Comparison (classical). The diagram uses boxes, arrows, and stylized wave representations. The man's hands are visible at the bottom, using a blue pen to point at different parts of the flowchart. (6) The man is back on screen, speaking directly to the camera. He is holding the small remote in one hand and gestures with the other. The background environment is unchanged from previous talking-head segments. (7) A line graph is displayed. The y-axis is labeled OTOC and the x-axis is Time in milliseconds. Three data sets are plotted: Ideal (red circles), Raw (gray squares), and Mitigated (blue diamonds). The Ideal and Mitigated plots follow a similar decaying curve, while Raw decays much faster. The man's hand with the blue pen points to the Mitigated data points. (8) Final segment with the man speaking. He continues his energetic delivery, using his hands and the remote frequently. He smiles towards the end. The yawning cat and the blurred interior remain in the background until the video ends.
visual_base.text_narrative_log: (1) [Slogan]: 鎖定思想實驗室 提升你的見識. [Subtitle]: Google 的量子電腦「有用」了. [Logo]: Google. (2) [Subtitle]: 他們在《Nature》剛發表的研究展示了「量子回聲」這個新演算法. (3) [Subtitle]: 是第一次在「實際可驗證」的任務上展現量子優勢. (4) [Subtitle]: 科學家一直想用電腦模擬分子結構. (5) [Subtitle]: 但分子裡的量子糾纏太複雜. (6) [Subtitle]: 雖然傳統的「核磁共振」NMR 技術可量出分子結構. (7) [Subtitle]: 但看不清楚那種有好幾個環的大型分子中遠距離原子的互動. (8) [Subtitle]: 訊號糊成一團. (9) [Subtitle]: 如果交給超級電腦去模擬得算幾萬年. (10) [Subtitle]: Google 想到一招. (11) [Subtitle]: 他們在自家的「Willow」量子晶片上先對某個量子位元下指令. (12) [Subtitle]: 就像在峽谷裡大喊一聲當作標記. (13) [Subtitle]: 接著讓整個量子系統自然演化. (14) [Subtitle]: 讓這個聲音也就是量子資訊像漣漪一樣擴散出去. (15) [Subtitle]: 演化到一半他們在另一頭「戳一下」遠處的量子位元製造一點擾動. (16) [Subtitle]: 好比有人突然敲了鑼. (17) [Subtitle]: 然後他們讓整個系統時間倒轉彷彿按下倒帶鍵. (18) [Subtitle]: 最後再去檢查最初那個被標記的位元看「回聲」能不能完美重現. (19) [Subtitle]: 如果能表示那聲鑼沒什麼影響. (20) [Subtitle]: 但如果回聲變了就代表量子資訊在中途被擾亂. (21) [Subtitle]: 而「變化的程度」就是要測的物理量叫做 OTOC 亂序時間相關函數. (22) [Subtitle]: 厲害的是他們能把這套「演化－擾動－倒帶」的流程來回跑好幾次. (23) [Subtitle]: 去量更複雜的量子關係. (24) [Subtitle]: 他們用 65 個量子位元跑 23 個週期的 OTOC 測量. (25) [Subtitle]: 速度比全球最強的超級電腦 Frontier 硬是快了 13000 倍. (26) [Subtitle]: 好這方法是有了但怎麼用在分子結構模擬呢. (27) [Subtitle]: Google 和 UC Berkeley 合作用這個新演算法幫忙解核磁共振的近視難題. (28) [Subtitle]: 把量子回聲當成「超精密分子尺」. (29) [Subtitle]: 測試對象是兩種有機分子甲苯 (C7H8) 跟一個更複雜的 DMBP (3',5'-二甲基聯苯). (30) [Subtitle]: 傳統核磁共振量到 DMBP 這種分子時圖譜裡的訊號全糊在一起. (31) [Subtitle]: 很難反推出兩個環到底扭了幾度. (32) [Subtitle]: 他們就把量出來的那真實但很糊的訊號當作「考題」. (33) [Subtitle]: 接著在量子電腦上「猜」一個結構. (34) [Subtitle]: 例如「我猜兩個環扭轉 30 度」. (35) [Subtitle]: 然後用「量子回聲」去模擬如果分子真的長這樣它理論上的訊號會長怎樣. (36) [Subtitle]: 最後把模擬結果比對真實訊號. (37) [Subtitle]: 不像那就換個角度再猜直到模擬跟真實訊號完美吻合. (38) [Subtitle]: Bingo 這就是大分子的真實構型. (39) [Subtitle]: 換句話說「量子回聲」演算法給了近視的核磁共振聽聲辨位的新能力. (40) [Subtitle]: 不過量子電腦錯誤率很高不是嗎. (41) [Subtitle]: 沒錯所以 Google 團隊幾乎把能用的除錯技巧都用上了. (42) [Subtitle]: 他們使出「零噪音外推」法故意讓誤差變嚴重. (43) [Subtitle]: 再用數學反推出「零錯誤」時的理想結果. (44) [Subtitle]: 還請出 DeepMind 的 AI「AlphaEvolve」來自動改善量子電路找出最抗噪的路線. (45) [Subtitle]: 結果非常漂亮最終數據和理論值幾乎一模一樣誤差小得驚人. (46) [Subtitle]: 看來 Google 這次不再炫耀一些形式上的領先. (47) [Subtitle]: 而是證明量子電腦可以在科學研究裡發揮可驗證的優勢. (48) [Subtitle]: 為未來的新藥研發、材料設計開了大門. (49) [Subtitle]: 也為新一代量子偽科學產品提供了很多點子. (50) [Subtitle]: 例如量子回聲療癒誦經機啦量子回聲逆時無痕青春露啦. (51) [Subtitle]: OTOC 宇宙能量平衡儀等等. (52) [Subtitle]: 真的想買.
